title: Lanecheck prep - Vivian Park
content:
Context and goal:
This is a quick lane-check before my weekly sync with Ravi (eng lead). Focus is triage + unblock: API quota behavior with Console 2.1 rollout, Dedicated capacity commit decisions, and the initial Private-deploy pilot timeline for AcmeCorp. Leave the meeting with clear owners for infra changes and a go/no-go signal on the canary plan for console features.

Primary objectives:
- Confirm plan and SLOs for Console 2.1 rollout (canary targets, telemetry, rollback triggers).
- Align on Dedicated capacity pricing/commit ask for Q2 enterprise deals (what we can promise).
- Get a concrete Private deployment onboarding checklist for the Acme pilot (network, KMS, audit logs).
- Surface any infra risk that would push timeline >2 weeks.

Quick agenda (20-30m):
1) 5m - quick sync on last week's action items and metrics (latency 95p, error spikes).
2) 10m - Console 2.1 canary plan: targets + metrics + rollback criteria.
3) 7m - Dedicated commit: capacity numbers, risk, pricing guardrails.
4) 5m - Private pilot readiness + next steps.
5) 3m - confirm owners, due dates, and follow-ups.

Notes / talking points to open with:
- Start with two quick numbers: recent API tokenized-usage per customer (top 5) and 95p latency trend last 72h. If there was a spike, call it out immediately.
- Console 2.1 includes: improved model selector, per-route token accounting, and streaming diagnostics. The main risk is the new per-route accounting hook causing extra DB reads under high concurrency.
- Ask Ravi whether the new accounting hook can be sharded or cached with a TTL to avoid tail latency regressions.
- For Dedicated: sales wants to convert three POC customers (ACME, Nimbus, BrightLayer) into reserved commitments. We need to be conservative on promised TPS and CPU headroom.
- Private: Acme pilot needs KMS integration and audit-log export. Legal flagged retention requirements; engineering needs to confirm export format and retention APIs.

Metrics to have on hand (bring screenshots or links):
- API throughput (RPS) last 7 days, 95p token latency last 72h, error rate by route.
- DB query times for accounting hook (p95/p99).
- GPU utilization on Dedicated clusters (by pool) and average batch sizes.

Decisions I want by end of meeting:
- Canary targets for Console 2.1: 5% traffic for 48h, success if p95 latency delta <= +10% and errors not increased >0.5% absolute.
- Whether we use a cached accounting layer (temp) or proceed without caching in canary.
- Confirm committed Dedicated baseline (suggested: reserve 100 kTokens/sec equiv across 2 pools) or postpone to next week.
- Private pilot go/no-go for Acme: must have KMS + audit export + basic runbook.

Risks & mitigations to raise:
- Risk: accounting hook DB reads cause p99 latency tail in particular with small batches. Mitigation: enable a 30s in-memory TTL cache or degrade detailed per-request accounting to sampling.
- Risk: Dedicated commit too aggressive leading to underutilized GPUs and higher fixed costs for customers. Mitigation: propose staggered reserve with ramp-based billing for first 60 days.
- Risk: Private pilot network egress/firewall rules delay onboarding. Mitigation: pre-schedule a network sandbox session with Acme infra + our SREs this week.

Proposed action items (post-meeting owners + due dates):
- "Explore cached accounting layer feasibility" — Owner: Ravi Shah — Due: 2026-03-18 — Deliverable: short doc with bench numbers and ops impact.
- "Prepare Console 2.1 canary config" — Owner: Maya Lopez (Release Eng) — Due: 2026-03-16 — Deliverable: canary YAML + rollout playbook.
- "Draft Dedicated commit recommendation" — Owner: Vivian Park (me) + Kai Nguyen (finance) — Due: 2026-03-17 — Deliverable: recommended commit numbers + price band.
- "Private pilot checklist & runbook" — Owner: SRE rotation (TBD) — Due: 2026-03-19 — Deliverable: runbook + KMS integration steps + audit export spec.
- "Customer comms draft for Acme" — Owner: Customer Success (Maya) — Due: 2026-03-18 — Deliverable: email + kickoff agenda.

Open questions to push on in meeting:
- Can we run a synthetic load test that exercises the accounting hook at 2x observed peak within 48h? (If yes, request schedule).
- Is there appetite to include a temporary sampling fallback for per-route accounting if latency regresses?
- What pricing floor do we absolutely need to provide for Dedicated to satisfy Sales (Kai to confirm thresholds).

Notes to self (things to bring into meeting):
- Link to INF-4482 (console telemetry bug) and the PR that fixed the related race (GH #5178).
- Small table of top-5 customers by token usage (screenshot from dashboard).
- Example rollback playbook we used for v2.0 canary (copy).

Follow-ups after meeting (example templates):
- Quick Slack status to #product-and-eng with canary config + owners and next meeting time.
- Create follow-up JIRA tasks for each action item and assign with due dates.
- Book a 30m deep-dive on the accounting hook with infra and DB owners if Ravi wants more benching.

Tone & framing guidance for myself:
- Be concrete and data-driven (bring numbers) — Ravi responds best to perf numbers and clear trade-offs.
- Frame Dedicated asks as trial-to-commit (staggered ramp) not as immediate large fixed contracts.
- For Private, emphasize minimal scope for Acme pilot: KMS + audit export + one region, no custom integrations yet.

TODO (scratch):
- Pull customer top-5 usage table from dashboard (Vivian) — done? partial, finish before meeting.
- Slack Ravi a 1-line agenda 1 hour before the meeting.
- Attach the release playbook to the canary JIRA.

Quick revision history (notes-to-self):
- 2026-03-10 initial draft
- 2026-03-12 updated with latest p95 numbers and Added Dedicated pricing ask
- 2026-03-13 final prep edits (added Acme pilot checklist requirement)

Misc (brain dump):
- If canary shows small latency regression but no errors, consider enabling sampling for accounting for first 2 weeks then roll full accounting once we ship an optimized DB index.
- If Dedicated reserve is approved, propose a telemetry tag to track customers on reserved capacity vs. on-demand for cost analysis.

End of lane-check prep.
